Reliable Robotics adds $115 million to expand autonomous aviation development

The financing combines $90 million in equity and a $25 million loan for fleet and engineering growth while FAA certification continues.

TechStartups ↗20 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2

New capital and engineering expansion

Reliable Robotics announced $115 million in additional capital on October 20: $90 million in equity and a $25 million Silicon Valley Bank term loan. This brings the Series D total to $275 million and valuation above $1 billion. It plans to expand aircraft, production and engineering, with new Seattle and San Diego offices.

Retrofitting existing aircraft

The Reliable Autonomy System, or RAS, is being developed for automatic taxi, takeoff, en-route flight management and landing, with the Cessna 208B Grand Caravan as its certification platform. It adapts existing aircraft and aviation infrastructure while the company also develops radar to help address collision risks.

Financing is not operating approval

FAA certification remains in progress, so the funding does not mean unrestricted autonomous commercial service is approved. More aircraft and engineers support testing and safety evidence, while commercial expansion still depends on regulatory requirements and demonstrating consistent system performance.
